A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching classifiers and MNIST experiments. Their main texts, equations, figures, references, and complete Appendices A and B support reliable comparison; v2 explicitly identifies itself as a generalization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 5 report original experiments comparing image alignment and three CNN architectures on randomly deformed MNIST images.

after.justification: Section 5 and Figure 8 retain the original MNIST experiments, reporting median test errors over 30 repetitions.

M1.justification: V2 adds an inverse-mapping nearest-neighbor classifier that searches discretized transformations of training and test images. It generalizes the image model and CNN filter construction beyond scaling and shifting, and replaces least-squares CNN fitting with an objective described as empirical 0–1 risk minimization. The original support-alignment classifier remains.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same three MNIST tasks: single-template 0 versus 4, single-template 1 versus 7, and 0 versus 4 with ten templates per class. Rotations, nonlinear deformations, and cat illustrations expand the theory and exposition without adding evaluated dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The reported comparisons retain IAC, CNN1, CNN2, and CNN3 in all three tasks. Neither the new inverse-mapping classifier nor newly cited invariant-network methods enter the empirical comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the stated Adam learning rate from 0.01 to 0.001. The architecture variants, balanced training sizes of 2–64, 100-image test sets, and misclassification metric are retained. The PDFs do not establish whether the learning-rate revision reflects a correction or rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: The architecture comparison and multiple-template analysis already appear in v1. No new ablation, robustness experiment, or error analysis is reported. The new CNN diagrams and appendix function plots illustrate mechanisms and proofs.

E5.justification: Both versions report median test error over 30 repetitions. No seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other empirical uncertainty-reporting practices are added.

E6.justification: The three empirical result panels in v1 Figure 5 are reproduced unchanged in v2 Figure 8, preserving the numerical curves and rankings. Some numerical prose is shortened, but the corresponding results remain plotted; no new measured outcomes are reported.

T1.justification: V2 replaces point-sampled pixels with pixel integrals, introduces general deformation assumptions and covering lemmas, and adds Theorem 3.1 for inverse matching. Its alignment theorem drops the earlier Gamma-set and support-width restrictions under the revised model, with rewritten upper- and lower-bound proofs. The CNN argument changes from a least-squares square-root risk bound to a reported |Ad|^2 log^3(|Ad|) log(n)/n bound under a different fitting criterion, substantially revising Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the contribution from two procedures for a specific deformation model to three procedures covering general deformation classes. CNN guarantees are reframed around deformation complexity and joint sample-size/resolution asymptotics. Claims about explaining data augmentation and overparameterization become statements of potential.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly characterizes inverse matching as a computationally demanding theoretical benchmark, discusses the intractability of 0–1 optimization, and distinguishes CNN expressivity guarantees from explanations of learned features. It also explains why the reported bound grows with resolution when class separation shrinks and adds applicability restrictions for perspective transformations.

D1.justification: The reported Adam learning-rate value changes from 0.01 to 0.001. Keras/TensorFlow, optimizer, architecture, and data-generation disclosures otherwise remain substantially the same; no implementation package or new code/data access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning toward functional-data classification, affine and perspective transformations, and invariant/equivariant CNNs. New cited works include Delaigle and Hall, Cohen and Welling, and Marcos et al. Classification-risk, surrogate-loss, and VC-theory references also support the revised analysis.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, model description, CNN discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 3 and Appendix A gain separate general-deformation and alignment subsections, while related-work material is redistributed. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redesigns the illustrations: it adds pixel/deformation, ambiguity, CNN-invariance, and filter diagrams; redraws alignment as three stages; and adds lower-bound function plots in Appendix A. Earlier rectangular-support and Gamma-set proof sketches disappear. The empirical plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens the mathematical scope and improves explanations and illustrations. However, replacing v1's least-squares objective introduces a central inconsistency: v2 Eq. (27) rewards positive-label predictions without penalizing false positives for labels in {0,1}, while Eq. (94) incorrectly equates it with the 0–1 minimization required by Lemma B.8. Thus the revised CNN guarantee is unsupported for the estimator as defined. These presentation and scope benefits coexist with a substantive reliability problem, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
